title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ الددو يحاضر بمنبر الجمعة ويسجل "وقفات مع سورة التوبة"
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures from the Friday Pulpit and Records "Pauses with Sūrat al-Tawbah"
body_ar: ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء ورئيس جمعية المستقبل للدعوة والثقافة والتعليم ورئيس جامعة عبد الله بن ياسين محاضرة علمية هامة تحت عنوان: وقفات مع سورة التوبة بمنبر الجمعة في مسجد الذكر بتنسويلم مساء أمس الجمعة 21 جمادى الثانية 1433هـ الموافق: 11 مايو 2012. وقد جرت المحاضرة وسط حضور جماهيري كبير غصت به جوانب المسجد وامتلأت به الساحات المحيطة به، حيث توافد الحضور من الساعات الأولى من المساء، وتوالى قدومهم حتى قبيل المغرب، إذ اكتظ داخل المسجد والساحات الموالية له، قبل أن يلجأ الجمهور إلى بعض الحيطان المجاورة، لينتظموا في جلوسهم متعطشين لحضور الشيخ والاستماع لما سيلقيه على آذانهم من العلم الشرعي، وتحرى الحضور حتى أمن على دعاء الشيخ في نهاية المحاضرة التي استمرت حتى دخول وقت المغرب. وقد استأنف فضيلة الشيخ حديثه بالتذكير بمنزلة القرآن الكريم بين الكتب السماوية السابقة له، مؤكدا أنه تميز بكونه لم ينزل مرة واحدة واحدة؛ وإنما نزل منجما حسب الوقائع وحاجات الناس، وذلك لحكم بالغة أراد الله جل شأنه أن يثبت بها النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام والمؤمنين، حتى يطمئنوا مرة بعد أخرى بمعية الله لهم، وتشريعه ما يصلح أحوالهم ويحقق التمكين لدينه في الأرض، معرجا على أصناف الناس من الصراع بين الحق والباطل، ثم تعرض الشيخ لابتلاء الله للمؤمنين، مستعرضا مختلف النكبات التي تعترض السائرين على منهج الله الخالد، مبينا أن التعرض لها دلالة على السير في طريق المصلحين عبر التاريخ من لدن آدم إلى يومنا هذا، مؤكدا على بركة النكبات التي يختص الله بها من ارتضاهم لخدمة دينه. وصنف فضيلة الشيخ تلك النكبات إلى قسمين كبيرين هما الخوف ونقص الثقة؛ وسرد في كل جزء القضايا المتعلقة به؛ حيث أكد أن الخوف يشمل الخوف من أعداء الله وخططهم وصولتهم المضمحلة عما قريب، كما يشمل الخوف على المصالح مذكرا بقوله تعالى في هذه السورة: "وإن خفتم عيلة فسوف يغنيكم الله من فضله" ومنه الخوف من التشويه الذي قد يأتي في صورة من الحرص على بذل النصح وتقديم الحكمة في سبيل التبرم من تبعات سلوك طريق الحق. ونبه فضيلة الشيخ إلى أن الخوف يمتد أيضا ليشمل الخوف من التكاليف بقصرها على الحفاظ على النفس وحراسة المال، وهما قد اشتراهما الله تعالى من المؤمنين مقابل جنة عرضها السماوات والأرض، مذكرا بانقسام الناس حيال البيعة مع الله إلى صادقين ومنافقين، وهو النفاق العملي الذي يصدق على كل من لم يف بالبيعة مع الله عز وجل، ومن الخوف أيضا الخوف من المجهول، وهنا أورد الشيخ قصة بني إسرائيل الواردة في سورة المائدة حين قالوا لموسى: "اذهب أنت وربك فقاتلا إنا ههنا قاعدون" وتفادي هذا الخوف يقتضي من المسلم ضرورة التأقلم مع تطور الأمم والحضارة ومواكبة سرعة الاكتشاف التكنولوجي للسير بمستوى التغيير المتصاعد في هذا العصر، أما نقص الثقة فيضم نقص الثقة في النفس الذي يؤدي إلى الاعتذار بالانشغال وتكاثر هموم الحياة ثم نقص الثقة في العاملين الذي ينتج عن بعض أمراض النفس وضعف البصيرة والقياس على التجارب الفاشلة، ومنه عدم الثقة في القيادة وفي المستقبل بتوقع تراجع الأمور وتفاقم الوضع؛ وهذا هو ظن السوء المنهي عنه في الآية الكريمة، حيث سرد الشيخ العديد من النصوص الشرعية المؤكدة للتمكين للدين وصيرروة الأمور لصالح الإسلام وناصريه، ثم انتقل الشيخ إلى عدم الثقة في المنهج بسبب التخبط بين مناهج البشر المتناقضة، ومتوقفا مع بعض آثار التخلف عن منهج الحق وتكاليفه، مستدلا ببعض القضايا التي تستحق التوقف من الأحداث التي جرت على هامش غزوة تبوك التي فضحت المنافقين وأعذارهم في التراجع والتخلف عن نصرة دين الإسلام. للمتابعة اضغط هنا:
body_en:
Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew — president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, president of the Future Association for Calling to Islam, Culture and Education, and president of Abdullah ibn Yasin University — delivered an important scholarly lecture under the title "Pauses with Sūrat al-Tawbah" from the Friday pulpit at the Mosque of Remembrance in Tensweilim, on the evening of yesterday, Friday 21 Jumada al-Thaniyah 1433 AH, corresponding to 11 May 2012.

The lecture took place amid a large public attendance which filled the sides of the mosque to overflowing and filled the squares surrounding it. Those attending began arriving from the first hours of the evening and continued to come until shortly before sunset, so that the inside of the mosque and the squares adjoining it were packed, before the crowd resorted to some of the neighbouring walls, arranging themselves in their seating, thirsting to be present with the Sheikh and to hear what he would deliver to their ears of the knowledge of the Sharia. Those present persevered to the point of saying amen to the Sheikh's supplication at the close of the lecture, which continued until the time of the sunset prayer came in.

The Sheikh resumed his talk by recalling the standing of the Noble Qur'an among the revealed books that preceded it, affirming that it is distinguished by not having been sent down all at once, but rather having been sent down in instalments according to events and to people's needs — and that for consummate wisdoms by which God, exalted be His station, willed to make the Prophet, upon him be blessings and peace, and the believers firm, so that they might be reassured time after time by God's being with them and by His legislating what sets their affairs right and brings about the establishment of His religion in the earth. He touched upon the classes into which people fall in the struggle between truth and falsehood.

The Sheikh then took up God's testing of the believers, reviewing the various calamities that confront those who walk upon God's everlasting way, explaining that being met with them is an indication of walking in the path of the reformers throughout history, from Adam down to our own day, and affirming the blessing in the calamities with which God singles out those whom He has chosen for the service of His religion.

The Sheikh classified those calamities into two large divisions — fear, and deficiency of confidence — and in each part he set out the matters pertaining to it. He affirmed that fear takes in fear of God's enemies, of their schemes and of their assault, which will shortly dwindle away; and that it takes in fear for one's interests too, recalling the word of God Most High in this sura: "And if you fear poverty, God will enrich you from His bounty". Among it is fear of being defamed, which may come in the guise of an eagerness to give sincere advice and to offer wisdom, in the service of a weariness at the consequences of walking the path of truth.

The Sheikh pointed out that fear extends also to take in fear of the obligations laid down by the law, by confining them to the preservation of one's life and the guarding of one's property — and God Most High has bought both of these from the believers in exchange for a garden whose breadth is the heavens and the earth. He recalled the division of people, faced with the pledge with God, into the truthful and the hypocrites; and this is hypocrisy in deed, which holds true of everyone who has not fulfilled the pledge with God, mighty and majestic.

Among the forms of fear too is fear of the unknown, and here the Sheikh cited the story of the Children of Israel that comes in Sūrat al-Māʾidah, when they said to Moses: "Go, you and your Lord, and fight; we shall sit here." Averting this fear requires of the Muslim that he adapt to the development of nations and of civilisation and keep pace with the speed of technological discovery, so as to move at the level of the mounting change of this age.

As for deficiency of confidence, it takes in a deficiency of confidence in oneself, which leads to pleading preoccupation and the multiplying of life's cares as an excuse; then a deficiency of confidence in those who do the work, which arises from certain diseases of the soul, from weakness of insight, and from reasoning by analogy from failed experiences. Among it too is a lack of confidence in the leadership and in the future, by expecting matters to regress and the situation to worsen — and this is the evil supposition forbidden in the noble verse. The Sheikh set out many of the texts of the Sharia affirming the establishment of the religion and the turning of affairs in favour of Islam and of those who give it victory.

The Sheikh then moved on to a lack of confidence in the method, owing to floundering among the contradictory methods of human beings, pausing with some of the effects of holding back from the method of truth and from its obligations, and adducing some of the matters that merit pausing over among the events that took place on the margins of the Tabuk expedition, which exposed the hypocrites and their excuses for retreating and for holding back from giving victory to the religion of Islam.

flags.arabic: ومنه الخوف من التشويه الذي قد يأتي في صورة من الحرص على بذل النصح وتقديم الحكمة في سبيل التبرم من تبعات سلوك طريق الحق
flags.context: the third kind of fear, in the news desk's summary
options: fear of being defamed, which may come in the guise of an eagerness to give sincere advice and to offer wisdom, in the service of a weariness at the consequences of walking the path of truth
fear of being defamed, which may take the form of an eagerness to counsel and to be prudent, out of impatience with the consequences of walking the path of truth
fear of distorting [the message], which may come in the form of ...
flags.note: The Arabic of this clause does not parse cleanly and the English is correspondingly strained. 'في سبيل' normally means 'for the sake of' and here yields something close to 'the eagerness to advise is a cover for weariness' — a sharp and interesting point, that caution dressed as wisdom is really fear — but the construction is loose enough that a reviewer may read it otherwise, and التشويه may be being defamed by others or distorting the message oneself. Nothing has been smoothed over: the English keeps the awkwardness rather than choosing a reading and writing it out confidently.

flags.context: among the causes of deficiency of confidence in those who do the work
options: reasoning by analogy from failed experiences
flags.note: HOMONYM WARNING. قياس is in the glossary as qiyās, 'analogical reasoning', a source of law in usul al-fiqh. That is emphatically not the sense here: this is ordinary reasoning from one's own bad experiences to a general distrust of colleagues. Deliberately not bracketed with the glossary term, which would turn a remark about workplace cynicism into a point of legal theory.

flags.context: the division of people faced with the pledge with God
flags.note: The distinction being invoked is a load-bearing one in creed: nifāq ʿamalī, hypocrisy in conduct, which is a grave sin, as against nifāq iʿtiqādī, hypocrisy in belief, which takes a person out of Islam. The report says that hypocrisy in deed 'holds true of everyone who has not fulfilled the pledge with God' — a very wide statement, and one whose safety depends entirely on the qualifier 'in deed'. The qualifier has been kept prominent in the English. Neither term is in the glossary and both should be added. A reader who loses the distinction will read this as a charge of unbelief, which it is not.

options: read as لم ينزل مرة واحدة, 'was not sent down all at once'
flags.note: The word واحدة is duplicated in the source. The sentence makes sense only without the duplication and the contrast that follows ('but rather in instalments') confirms it. Preserved in body_ar, rendered once in body_en, flagged rather than fixed.

flags.context: النصوص الشرعية المؤكدة للتمكين للدين وصيرروة الأمور لصالح الإسلام
flags.note: Source typo: an extra rāʾ in صيرورة. Preserved and flagged.

flags.arabic: "وإن خفتم عيلة فسوف يغنيكم الله من فضله" ... "اذهب أنت وربك فقاتلا إنا ههنا قاعدون"
flags.context: two Qur'anic quotations given without references
options: render and record the references in a note
render and insert the references in the body
flags.note: The first is Sūrat al-Tawbah 9:28 — the news desk correctly says it is in 'this sura' — and the second is Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:24, which the desk locates by sura but not by verse. The references are recorded here rather than inserted into the body: the quotations are the desk's, given in plain quotation marks, and style guide section 4's citation convention is for the Sheikh's own quotation of scripture. Renderings are interpretive and are no substitute for the Arabic. The record alludes without quoting to Sūrat al-Tawbah 9:111 (God's purchase of the believers' lives and property) and to Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:133 (a garden whose breadth is the heavens and the earth).

flags.arabic: وقد جرت المحاضرة وسط حضور جماهيري كبير ... حتى دخول وقت المغرب
flags.context: the second paragraph, against the second paragraph of record 797
options: treat as boilerplate and abridge one
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT, of a kind worth tracking corpus-wide. This entire paragraph is word-for-word identical with the corresponding paragraph of record 797 in this same slice, a lecture at the same mosque five weeks later; 797's copy carries an extra ellipsis. It is house boilerplate for 'a lecture at the Mosque of Remembrance', not a report of this particular evening. Both have been translated in full, since the style guide forbids summarising; but the site should not present the crowd description as observation, and a duplicate-text scan across the news section is likely to find more.

translator_notes: A news-desk report, not a transcript; the lecture itself exists only as a recording that the record points to and the corpus does not hold. The summary is unusually detailed and follows the lecture's structure closely, which makes it more tempting than most to read as his words. It is not.
The CMS timestamp, 12 May 2012, is a bulk-upload date; the body dates the lecture to the evening of Friday 21 Jumada al-Thaniyah 1433 / 11 May 2012.
'تنسويلم' is Tensweilim, a district of Nouakchott; 'مسجد الذكر' is rendered 'the Mosque of Remembrance', dhikr being the remembrance of God.
'غزوة تبوك' is rendered 'the Tabuk expedition'. Sūrat al-Tawbah is closely bound to that campaign, which is why the lecture ends there.
'وقفات' in the title is the established Arabic genre-word for a set of reflective pauses on a text; 'Pauses' keeps it rather than inflating it to 'Reflections'.
